title: Reselling Shared AI Platform Subscriptions:Business Models and Pricing Strategies in the Algerian Market
content: The proliferation of artificial intelligence (AI) tools has transformed academic practices worldwide, offering functionalities ranging from plagiarism detection to content generation. In Algeria, local vendors such as DzPlagiarism.in, AiZair, Academic Ai Tools, Fikra Academy, and ChatGPT Plus DZ provide accessible AI solutions tailored to students, faculty, and researchers. To better understand how these vendors operate and how AI tools are adopted in higher education, we conducted this study to examine their pricing strategies, service quality, risk compliance, and business models, as well as user perceptions and adoption patterns. Publicly available data from vendor websites, social media pages, and user comments were analyzed to assess affordability, accessibility, and user satisfaction. A thematic content analysis categorized feedback into areas such as delivery speed, reliability, support, price satisfaction, refunds, and security concerns. Results indicate a wide variation in pricing models, from subscription-based packages to freemium and educational models, reflecting adaptation to local economic conditions. User feedback highlights differences in service quality, with some vendors praised for usability and responsiveness, while others faced criticism for complex interfaces and limited support. Risk assessment revealed compliance and transparency gaps, particularly regarding shared accounts, which may contravene software Terms of Service and raise ethical concerns. The study underscores the need for institutional support, training, and clear ethical guidelines to facilitate effective AI adoption in Algerian universities. Findings contribute to understanding how AI vendors target academic markets in emerging economies and offer insights for policymakers, educators, and vendors to promote equitable, ethical, and sustainable use of AI tools in higher education.
